summary: PhysicsLabScale still lacks a primitive-number preflight before numeric operators. On main and generation-5 PR #389, assertFinite(value) begins with value == value and ordering against math.huge; a metatable-backed non-number can therefore reach caller-controlled comparison metamethods before rejection. PR #389 adds derived-output finiteness checks but does not close this input no-execute boundary. The existing scale test covers NaN/infinity/output overflow only, not hostile non-number inputs. Absorb a narrow type(value) == 'number' preflight plus adversarial no-metamethod regressions into the retained geometry lineage before integration; no new lane or architecture is needed.
evidence: main@ae83c0ef470eb2e73d99be41fd3561ede30c40e1 src/shared/Physics/PhysicsLabScale.luau assertFinite performs value == value and value >/-< math.huge without first checking type(value) == 'number'.
PR #389 patch at exact head 3c8c041d557a84202b35ff63fd0ec82478836401 only adds assertFinite() on converted outputs; it leaves the input assertFinite implementation unchanged.

main tests/physics_lab_scale.luau covers exact vectors, round-trip, NaN, and infinity. PR #389 adds finite meter->stud overflow coverage; neither current main nor the PR patch adds hostile metatable-backed input coverage.
Repository PR search for PhysicsLabScale/metatable/no-execute returned no separate active repair, so this does not duplicate an existing scale boundary lane.
